title: PHON: A Domain-Specific Language for Photonic Circuit Design and Optical Neural Network Inference
description:
PHON is an open-source DSL for photonic circuit design and optical neural network inference. A single source compiles to: (1) a Python simulation, (2) GDSII layout (viewable in KLayout), (3) neural network inference via layer/propagate primitives with relu/sigmoid/softmax/linear activations, and (4) an ONNX surrogate for fast parameter sweeps.

Current v0.10.0 supports photonic (optical) media only. Phononic (acoustic) support is planned for Phase 5.5 via a unified medium kind attribute, which will dispatch physics constants (refractive index, sound velocity) without changing the computation.

As of v0.10.0, the MNIST PoC achieves 97.78% test accuracy with 0 mismatches versus scikit-learn on a 100-sample audit set. A companion pipeline (PHON-LLM, separate repository) provides natural-language frontends: 135M LoRA-tuned code generation with constrained decoding (98% syntax validity on 50-prompt eval) and hybrid parameter extraction (regex-first + Qwen-0.5B/Outlines CFG fallback, 100% on curated and novel eval sets).

History: PHON was originally developed as a phononic (acoustic) DSL in early versions; it was later expanded to photonic circuits. v0.10.0 focuses on photonic design and optical neural network inference. A unified medium-agnostic DSL (photonic + phononic) is planned for Phase 5.5, not yet implemented.

Scope disclaimer: v0.10.0 simulates wave propagation and neural network inference on CPU using numpy. It is not a physical photonic or phononic hardware implementation, nor a compiler to real photonic/SAW hardware primitives. Claims of "wave-based AI" refer to the simulation framework, not deployed hardware.
